page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz, with 1 physical core and 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The CPU includes hardware flags such as AVX, AVX-512, and AES cryptography support.

In benchmark evaluations, the n2-standard-2 demonstrates entry-level performance characteristics. Its single-core stress-ng score of 1398.19 and Geekbench single-core score of 1123.0 are categorized as weak, while multi-core performance metrics, such as a Geekbench multi-core score of 1333.0, fall into the poor category. Memory bandwidth is measured at 102.01 GB/sec for cached small blocks and drops to 13.8 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Single-threaded gzip compression is a relative highlight, performing at an average tier of 23.81 GB/sec, whereas tasks like software compilation, ray tracing, and database operations score in the bottom 10% of tested hardware.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-standard-2 offers a low-cost entry point for dedicated-vCPU computing without the performance variability of burstable instances. Given its modest compute and memory footprint, along with its low benchmark scores in database operations and web serving throughput, this instance is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads. Appropriate use cases include basic development environments, low-traffic web serving, simple text processing, and small-scale utility applications that do not require high memory bandwidth or intensive multi-core processing.

This instance provides a cost-effective, dedicated-resource option for lightweight workloads such as basic development environments, low-traffic web serving, and simple text processing tasks.
